geometry.locator: arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2 "JUNO experimental site"; arXiv:1507.05613 Sec. 1.3.1 "Experimental site"
geometry.note: Representation is 'surveyed' (coordinate published by the collaboration) but confidence is kept 'approximate': the coordinate carries arc-second rounding, a stated ~60 m design shift and an ~100 m disagreement with the baselines (see notes).
geometry.quote: The geographic location is 112° 31’05” E and 22° 07’05” N.

method: Coordinate published by the JUNO Collaboration (arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2, repeated in arXiv:1507.05613 Sec. 1.3.1): 112°31'05" E, 22°07'05" N converted to decimal degrees as 112 + 31/60 + 5/3600 and 22 + 7/60 + 5/3600. Arc-second rounding alone is ~21 m; accuracy_m is set to 150 m because the same paper states the hall was moved ~60 m from its design position, does not say which position the quoted coordinate describes or its datum, and the published core baselines imply a position ~100 m SSW of this point (see notes).
name: JUNO underground experimental hall (published coordinate)
notes: Cross-check: the distance from this point to the centroid of each of the six Yangjiang reactor buildings and the two Taishan buildings is within 0.2 % (<= 101 m) of the GPS-surveyed baselines of arXiv:2104.02565 Table 1 (see geometry:juno-baseline-hall-point checks); the Taishan distances agree to <= 16 m, the six Yangjiang ones are all 96-101 m longer (a spread of 5 m), i.e. the baselines would put the detector ~100 m closer to Yangjiang (about SSW) than the published coordinate does. The offset is within accuracy_m but is reported rather than hidden.

summary.plain: The published position of the JUNO underground experimental hall under Dashi Hill, near Kaiping, Guangdong. A point, not a footprint: the hall's orientation and outline are not published as coordinates.
